pred_ddx.label: Sickle Cell Disease with Vaso-Occlusive Crisis

Sickle Cell Disease with Lymphadenopathy: The patient has Sickle Cell Anemia (Hb SS) and presents with significant lymph node enlargement, which is a known complication of the disease. The presence of hyperplasia of the paracortex with abundance of plasma cells and large epithelioid histiocytes containing lymphoid cells within their cytoplasm supports this diagnosis.
Sickle Cell Disease with Vaso-Occlusive: The patient has a history of Sickle Cell Anemia (Hb SS) and has experienced an acute vaso-occlusive crisis, which is a common complication of the disease. The presence of multiple enlarged lymph nodes throughout the abdomen further supports this diagnosis.
